headline: Blender’s Interface Escapes the Blender Shell
lede: BUI extracts Blender’s widget system into a standalone native runtime for Python, Rust, JavaScript, C, and C++. The project trades browser overhead for damage-based redraws, compact binaries, and a familiar power-user vocabulary—still with bindings and platforms under construction.

headline: A Bank Turns Android Choice Into a Liability
lede: ASN Bank’s app reportedly blocks devices running GrapheneOS and other non-Google Android systems, even when the application itself works. Behind the integrity check is a quieter question: when security proxies are platform controls, who gets to decide which customers count as trustworthy?

headline: An AI Coding Tool Leaked Its User’s Identity
lede: Claude Code reportedly placed a user’s email address in the User-Agent header sent to websites during web searches. The incident turns an implementation detail into a governance problem: agents need technical boundaries, not merely instructions to behave.
pullquote: Agents should not turn private account details into routine web traffic.

headline: Wood Ants Persist Inside an Impossible Pitfall
lede: A study follows a colony of red wood ants trapped for years in a deep underground bunker. With sunlight and ordinary food sources absent, scavenging, cannibalism, and social organization extended survival far beyond the species’ usual conditions.

headline: Kugelblitz Builds a Private Window Onto Earth
lede: Kugelblitz is a Mac-native 3D atlas for Earth, the Moon, Mars, and other worlds, powered by streamed open geodata. It combines terrain, buildings, historical events, local caching, and SpaceMouse navigation without requiring an account.

headline: A Long Password Can Open a Locked SSH Account
lede: OpenSSH on musl-based systems mishandled passwords longer than 256 characters, potentially bypassing accounts whose password field was meant to disable login. Update to OpenSSH 10.6p2, disable password authentication, and inspect Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot, and Yocto deployments.

headline: Microsoft Paint Carries an Unexplained RCE Warning
lede: CVE-2026-83844 associates Microsoft Paint with a reported remote-code-execution vulnerability, but the public record offers almost no exploit detail. Until the path is clear, the sensible response is plain: treat untrusted files carefully and watch for vendor guidance.

headline: Unleash Keeps Feature Rollouts Under Command
lede: Eleven years in, Unleash remains an open-source control plane for gradual releases, canaries, experiments, and kill switches. Self-host it, call it through APIs, and change production behavior without redeploying the application.

headline: Learn Security by Breaking Things on Purpose
lede: pwn.college turns cybersecurity education into a sequence of terminal challenges, lectures, and belt-level dojos. Its open infrastructure supports classrooms and independent learners while preserving selected exercises for the moment of discovery.

headline: Four Flaws Put Tata’s Connected Cars at Risk
lede: CERT-In lists four high-severity issues in Tata Motors’ iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev applications, including hardcoded credentials, exposed tokens, unsafe WebViews, and ineffective certificate pinning. Users should update both apps to the fixed releases.
